failures.criterion: The invariant the architect named for this round: every person's decision reaches its architect once, none lost
failures.evidence: Red test TestADecisionAStaleStartReleasesReachesTheRunningArchitect (packages/daemon/internal/daemon/parked_decision_test.go, commit 2f9a32bebb12). Command: `cd packages/daemon && LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... go test -count=1 -run TestADecisionAStaleStartReleasesReachesTheRunningArchitect ./internal/daemon/` -> FAIL: `after the stale start released dispatch://LEGION-1/ask/ask-1, no start or catch-up of LEGION-1 names it: generation 3's running architect is never told the person's decision`. Reproduced first on the whole daemon (TestTesterStaleStartReleaseLive, real PostgreSQL and NATS): a person's answer on a parked root is kept; re-admission's start A (generation 2) claims it and its architect resume keeps failing (row 59, 3 attempts, backoff); the tree is parked and re-admitted again, so start B (generation 3) runs at once, names nothing (the answer is claimed by A, B's task is empty), and resumes the architect; the architect reports ready and its catch-up leaves the claimed answer out; A then retries, logs `outbox supervise row serves an earlier generation; finished without acting`, and its finish releases the claim (on delete set null). Result: the answer is kept and unclaimed, named 0 times to the generation-3 architect, which is running (state ready), and nothing queued will name it; only the architect's next relaunch or the tree's next re-admission would. The state table's step 5 ('released back to KEPT, so the next start or catch-up names it') has no next start or catch-up when the architect is already running. Supervise rows of one issue are not run in row order (record/store.go outboxInOrder's comment: 'Supervise rows need no other such rule'), so an older start retrying behind a newer one is an ordinary state. A fix has to hand a released decision to a root whose architect runs (queue a catch-up when a claiming row of a live root finishes without delivering, or let a newer start or catch-up name rows claimed by a row of an earlier generation).

The implementer's trickyParts says an issue's outbox rows run in row order; for supervise rows they do not (record/store.go outboxInOrder). DeliveredThrough would suppress an older start row that retries after a newer one delivered; I found no path that queues a second architect start of the same generation while one is queued (boot rule-resume skips the architect and any role with a queued start; awaiting_person needs no start queued), so I record it rather than fail it. The failure above is the same ordering's other face.
